blocks.text: A Private Access (ZPA) user portal can display links to applications that your end users are authorized to access, as well as links to public applications or websites that your organization commonly uses.

After an end user logs in to a user portal and is authenticated via single sign-on (SSO), an acceptable use policy (AUP) can be displayed before they can access the policy. If an AUP is displayed, your end users must read and accept the policy terms.

After an end user logs in, the user portal home page appears. A list of all applications available to them is displayed based on the access policies for the application segments, which can be launched directly from the portal. Any applications with a policy rule set to Deny are not visible to the end user.
The user portal for Browser Access is dependent on the Default Timeout Policy rule's authentication timeout.
The following image shows the main user portal features.
Any messages from an admin are displayed at the top of the page, and can be dismissed by an end user if they click the Close icon.
An end user can click a link to launch an application. The user portal displays the following application link types, which are denoted by an icon:

blocks.item: - Denotes private (i.e., internal) applications that can only be accessed via Zscaler Client Connector.
- Denotes private web applications that can be accessed via your web browser (i.e., Browser Access).
- Denotes public (i.e., SaaS) web applications or other public websites.

blocks.text: By default, all link types are displayed but an end user can filter the list using the drop-down menu.

If a link is displayed but is inactive (i.e., grayed out), then an end user cannot launch it directly from the portal and might require a native client for that specific application (e.g., SSH, RDP, etc.). In addition to the native client, the end user also needs to have Zscaler Client Connector installed and enrolled on that device. To learn more, see End User Guides and What Is Zscaler Client Connector? If they do not have Zscaler Client Connector installed, you can give them the ability to download Zscaler Client Connector from the portal. To learn more, see Viewing and Managing Zscaler Client Connector Download Links.
